shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading away my only A for a second B would leave me with 0 A, 1 C, 2 B — reducing variety and utility since I already value diversity. Current equal holdings (1,1,1) are ideal; this trade unbalances my bundle.

Current inventory is A:1, C:1, B:1 - a perfectly balanced bundle. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with A:2, C:1, B:0, which reduces variety and lowers my utility since I value diversity across goods equally.

Trading away my only B would leave me with 0 B and 3 A, hurting variety. Current bundle (1,1,1) is already balanced; going to (3,1,0) reduces diversity value even though total goods stay similar. I'd rather keep balance or negotiate a trade that doesn't zero out a good.

Trading away my C to get B would leave me with 2B, 0C, 1A - reducing variety instead of increasing it. Since I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of all goods, this trade would create an imbalance rather than improve it. I'd rather keep balanced holdings or trade to gain a good I have less of.
Current inventory is 1 each of A, C, B, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, reducing variety and utility. Not beneficial.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 more C would leave me with 1 A, 3 C, 0 B - a highly unbalanced bundle that reduces variety and utility, even though total goods increase. I'd rather keep variety intact.

Trading away my only A (going to 0) while B increases from 1 to 2 would create imbalance, leaving me with 0 A, 1 C, 2 B. This reduces variety utility since I'd have none of one good. Current equal distribution (1,1,1) is already balanced; this trade would hurt more than help.

Current inventory is 1A/1C/1B, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for another A would make me 2A/1C/0B, which is less diverse and reduces utility given my preference for variety. I'd rather keep balance or trade to increase variety, not decrease it.

This trade would leave me with A:3, C:1, B:0, creating a highly imbalanced inventory. I value variety, so giving up my only B (going to 0) while stacking up A to 3 is worse than my current balanced holdings. I'd rather trade to even out quantities than concentrate in one good.
Current inventory is balanced at 1 each (A, C, B). Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Not beneficial.
I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, reducing variety and utility rather than improving it.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 1 A, 3 C, 0 B - losing variety entirely and creating a heavy imbalance toward C. Since I value variety, this reduces my utility rather than improving it.

Currently I have A:1, C:2, B:0. Trading away my only A for a B would leave me with A:0, C:2, B:1 - still an imbalanced bundle with a zero good. Since I value variety, giving up my sole unit of A (which I have least of, tied with B at 0) isn't ideal since A and B are both scarce for me. Trading my only A means I'd still have a 0-count good, just switching which one is zero, so no real gain in variety balance. Better to hold out for a trade that fills my B without depleting A.
I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading away a surplus C for a scarce B improves variety and balances my inventory (A:1, C:1, B:1), increasing overall utility.

Giving up 2C for 1B would leave me with A:1, C:0, B:1 — losing all C variety while only gaining 1 unit of B. Trading 2 for 1 is inefficient; I'd rather propose a 1-for-1 swap to gain variety without giving up too much value.
I have 3 A, 1 C, 0 B. Trading a surplus A for a B increases variety, moving my bundle toward a more balanced distribution (2 A, 1 C, 1 B), which increases my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with A:1, C:1, B:1, which is a nicely balanced bundle, but the price is too steep - losing 2A for only 1B overvalues B relative to A. I'd rather propose a 1-for-1 trade instead, since that would still balance my inventory without overpaying.

I only have 1 C, giving it away would leave me with 0 C, going from equal variety issue to a worse imbalance (3 A, 0 C, 1 B). Trading C for B just shifts which good I have zero of, without net improvement. I'd rather keep C and acquire B using A instead, or get B without giving up my only C.
I currently hold equal amounts (1 each) of A, C, and B. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and utility rather than improving it.

This trade would take me from an even 1-1-1 bundle to 2A-1C-0B, reducing variety. Since I value variety, going to zero of B while doubling A doesn't improve my utility - it would make my bundle less balanced.

Current bundle is (A1,C1,B1), a balanced set which I value for variety. Trading away my only B for 2 more A would leave me with A3,C1,B0 - losing variety entirely and creating a strong imbalance (0 B). Since I value variety, this reduces my utility despite gaining quantity in A.
This trade would leave me with 1 A, 0 C, 2 B - trading away my only C for a second B reduces variety instead of improving it, since I'd go from equal 1-1-1 to an unbalanced 1-0-2 bundle.

Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 1A/2C/0B, reducing variety since I'd have zero of one good. Since I value variety, this trade doesn't improve my utility - it just shifts imbalance from C to B.

Current inventory is 1A/1C/1B, a balanced set which I value for variety. Trading away my only B for 2C would leave me with 1A/3C/0B, creating a lopsided bundle with zero B, which hurts my variety-based utility more than gaining an extra C helps.

Currently I have 1 A, 1 C, 0 B - completely lacking variety in B. Trading my A (which I have) for B (which I have none of) moves me to 0 A, 1 C, 1 B, giving me two distinct goods instead of an imbalanced set with zero B. This improves variety-based utility significantly.

Currently I have 1 A, 1 C, 0 B. Trading 1 C for 1 B gives me 1 A, 0 C, 1 B - moving from having zero B to having some B while giving up a C I have surplus of relative to variety. This creates a more balanced, varied bundle (1 A, 1 B) matching my preference for variety, improving utility.

Trading away my only A would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, just shifting the imbalance rather than improving variety. Currently I have A:1, C:2, B:0 - trading A for B would give A:0, C:2, B:1, which is still uneven and I'd lose my only unit of A. Better to keep A and seek a trade that uses my surplus C instead to acquire B, preserving diversity across all three goods."
Currently I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading a surplus C for a scarce B improves variety and balances my bundle toward (1,1,1) equally valued goods.

Giving up 2C for 1B would leave me with A:1, C:0, B:1, eliminating variety in C entirely. I'd rather trade only 1C for 1B to gain B while keeping some C, achieving better balance across all three goods.

Currently I have A:1, C:1, B:0. Trading away my only A for a B gives me A:0, C:1, B:1 - moving from one good with zero to a more balanced spread, and diversifying my holdings which I value given diminishing returns on goods I already have.

Currently I have 1 A, 1 C, 0 B - trading C (which I have) for B (which I lack) gives me 1 of each good, achieving perfect variety which maximizes my utility given equal valuation and preference for variety.

Giving up my only A (which I'd drop to 0) to get B (going 0 to 1) just swaps which good I'm missing, not a net gain in variety. Current bundle A:1,C:2,B:0 would become A:0,C:2,B:1 - still uneven with a zero. Better to seek a trade that gives me B without losing my only A, e.g. trading a C for B instead.
Currently I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading a surplus C for a scarce B improves diversity and balances my bundle toward (1A,1C,1B), increasing overall utility.

Giving up 2C for 1B would leave me with A:1, C:0, B:1 - losing all variety in C entirely, which hurts my variety-seeking utility. A better trade would be 1C for 1B to balance my holdings across A, C, and B.

Currently I have A:1, C:1, B:0 — an unbalanced bundle. Trading away 1 A (which I have some of) for 1 B (which I have none of) moves me toward a more even distribution across all three goods, increasing my utility given my preference for variety.

Trading 1C for 1B gives me 1A,0C,1B - same variety spread but since I value variety, moving from having 0 of B to 1 while reducing C from 1 to 0 keeps total distinct goods same (still missing one type), but B is currently my scarcest good (0), so acquiring it increases marginal utility more than losing a C I already have one of. This improves balance toward equal holdings across goods overall in future trades."
